questions.question: The profit earned by selling an article for ₹ 900 is twice the loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹ 450. At what price should the article be sold to make a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price when profit was earned = ₹900

Selling price when loss was incurred = ₹450

**Concept:**

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price

**Solution:**

⇒ Profit when selling price is ₹900 = ₹900 - Cost Price

questions.question: A principal becomes ₹ 19,683 in 3 years at 8 percent per annum compound interest, compounding annually. What is the principal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount after 3 years = ₹19,683

Rate of interest = 8%

Time = 3 years

**Concept:** 

A = P(1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾ where A is the amount, P is the principal, r is the rate of interest, n is the number of times the interest is compounded per year, and t is the time.

**Solution:**

⇒ ₹19,683 = P(1 + 8%/1)⁽¹×³⁾

⇒ Solving for P gives P = ₹15,625

Hence, the principal is ₹15,625.

questions.question: The average age of 30 men is 25 years. 5 new men of an average age of 30 years joined them. Find the average age of all the men put together.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average age of 30 men = 25 years

The number of new men = 5

The average age of new men = 30 years

**Concept:** 

Average = Sum of Observations/Number of Observations

**Solution:**

⇒ Total age of 30 men = 30 × 25 years = 750 years

⇒ Total age of 5 new men = 5 × 30 years = 150 years

⇒ Total age of all men = Total age of 30 men + Total age of 5 men = 750 + 150 = 900 years

⇒ Total number of men = 30 + 5 = 35

⇒ Average age of all men = Total age of all men/Total number of men

⇒ 900/35 = 180/7 = 25(5)/(7)​ years

**Therefore, the average age of all men is 25(5)/(7)​ years.**

questions.question: The population of a village during the first year increases by 5% and during the second year it diminishes by 5%. At the end of the second year its population was 9975. What was the population at the beginning of the first year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Population at the end of the second year = 9975

Increase in the first year = 5%

Decrease in the second year = 5%

**Concept:** 

Population at the beginning of the first year = Population at the end of the second year/([(100 + Increase%)/100] × [(100 - Decrease%)/100])

**Solution:**

⇒ Population at the beginning of the first year = 9975/([(100 + 5)/100] × [(100 - 5)/100])

⇒ 9975 × 100/105 × 100/95 = 10000

**Hence, the population at the beginning of the first year was 10,000.**

questions.question: If the length, breadth, and height of a cuboidal box are 24 cm, 16 cm, and 12 cm, respectively, then the volume of the box is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length = 24 cm

Breadth = 16 cm

Height = 12 cm

**Concept:** 

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

**Solution:**

⇒ Volume = 24 cm × 16 cm × 12 cm = 4608 cm³

**Therefore, the volume of the box is 4608 cm³.**

questions.question: If goods are purchased for Rs. 600 and one fifth is sold at a loss of 20%, at what gain percent should the remainder be sold so as to gain 30% on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of goods = ₹600

One fifth sold at a loss of 20%

Overall gain required = 30%

**Concept:** 

Gain% = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price × 100%

**Solution:**

⇒ Loss on selling one-fifth goods = 20% of (1/5 × ₹600)

⇒ Gain required on the total = 30% of ₹600

⇒ Gain required on remaining 4/5 goods = Gain on total + Loss on one-fifth

⇒ Gain% required on remaining goods = (Gain required on remaining goods/(4/5 × ₹600)) × 100%

**Therefore, the remainder should be sold at approximately a 42.5% gain.**

questions.question: What is the total surface area of a hemisphere of diameter 7 cm? Take π = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the hemisphere = 7 cm

Radius of the hemisphere = Diameter/2 = 7/2 cm

Pi(π) = 22/7

**Concept:** 

Total surface area of a hemisphere = 3πr²

**Solution:**

⇒ Total surface area = 3 × (22/7) × (7/2)² cm² = 115.5 cm²

**Hence, the total surface area of the hemisphere is 115.5 cm².**

questions.question: Find the HCF of 0.25, 2.08 and 8.1.
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

Numbers = 0.25, 2.08, 8.1

**Concept:** 

HCF of decimals can be found by multiplying the decimals by 10ⁿ (where n is the number of digits after the decimal in the number with the most decimal places), finding the

HCF of these numbers, then dividing by 10ⁿ.

**Solution:**

⇒ Multiply each number by 100 (as 2.08 has two digits after the decimal), to get 25, 208, and 810

⇒ HCF of 25, 208, and 810 is 1

⇒ Divide this HCF by 100 to get back to decimal form

**Therefore, the HCF of 0.25, 2.08, and 8.1 is 0.01.**

questions.question: The salary of an employee is first increased by 15% and then it is decreased by 25%. What is the percentage increase or decrease in his salary?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial increase = 15%

Decrease = 25%

**Concept:** 

Successive percentage change

**Solution:**

⇒ The net percentage change for two successive changes a and b is given by a + b + ab/100

⇒ Substitute a = 15 and b = -25 (decrease is taken as negative)

⇒ 15 - 25 - 375/100 = - 13.75%

**Therefore, there is a 13.75% decrease in the salary.**

questions.question: Mohan and Ramesh together can do a piece of work in 6 days, and Mohan alone can do it in 10 days. In how many days can Ramesh alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Mohan and Ramesh can do the work in 6 days

Mohan alone can do the work in 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work done = Efficiency × time

**Solution: **

Monan and Rames done work in 6 days.

Mohan alone can do same work alone in 10 days.

LCM of (6, 10) = 30.

Work done by both in 1 day = 30/6= 5 units.

Work done by Mohan in 1 day = 30/10 = 3 units.

Work done by Ramesh = 5 - 3 = 2 units

Time take by ramesh = 30/2 = 15 days

**Hence, Ramesh alone can do the same work in 15 days.**

questions.question: Find the greatest number by which, when numbers 47, 95 and 187 are divided, leave the same remainder in each case.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers = 47, 95, 187

**Concept used:**

The greatest number which when subtracted from given numbers leaves the same remainder is equal to HCF of the differences of the pairs of numbers

**Calculation:**

Let's find the differences:

95 - 47 = 48, 187 - 95 = 92, 187 - 47 = 140.

Now, we find the GCD of 48, 92, and 140.

Start by finding the GCD of two numbers:

GCD(48, 92) = 4, GCD(4, 140) = 4.

**So, the greatest number by which when numbers 47, 95, and 187 are divided, leaving the same remainder in each case, is 4.**

questions.question: Mohan and Sohan invested ₹ 6,000 and ₹ 8,000 respectively in a property simultaneously and after 6 months Sohan withdraws his invested amount. What is the ratio of money received by Mohan and Sohan respectively at the end of one year?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Mohan's investment = ₹6,000 for 12 months

Sohan's investment = ₹8,000 for 6 months

**Formula used:**

Returns are proportional to the product of the money invested and the time period of investment

**Solution:**

⇒ Mohan's product = ₹6,000 × 12

⇒ Sohan's product = ₹8,000 × 6

⇒ Ratio = Mohan's product: Sohan's product

**Hence, the ratio of money received by Mohan and Sohan respectively at the end of one year is 3 ∶ 2.**

questions.question: Anit can do a piece of work in 77 days. Ram can do the same work in 11 days. Ram and Anit start working together but Ram left the work 3 days before the completion of the work. Find the approximate number of days in which the work is completed.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Anit's = 77 days

Ram's = 11 days

Ram left 3 days before the completion

**Formula used:**

Work done = rate × time

**Solution:**

LCM of 77 and 11 is 77

Work done by Anit = 77/77 = 1

Work done by Ram = 77/11 = 7

Ram left the work 3 days, so make him do 3 days extra work which is equal to 3 × 7 = 21

Now total work = 77 + 21 = 98

Now work is completed in = 98/( 1 + 7) = 98/8 = 12.25 ≈ 12 days 

**Therefore, the work is completed in approximately 12 days.**

questions.question: A milkman bought 45 litres of milk and mixed 15 litres of water in it. If the price per litre of the mixture becomes ₹ 50, then what is the cost price of the milk per litre? (water is available free of cost)
questions.solution:
**Given**

Milk = 45 liters

Water = 15 liters (free)

Mixture price = ₹50 per liter

**Formula used:**

Cost of pure milk = (Cost of mixture ×Volume of mixture)/Volume of milk

**Solution:**

⇒ Cost of milk per liter = ₹50 × [(45 liters + 15 litres)/ (45 liters)] = ₹ 66(2)/(3)

**Therefore, the cost price of milk per liter is approximately ₹** 66(2)/(3)

questions.question: Vidhi gave Radha ₹ 8,000 on compound interest for 2 years at 5% per annum, compounding annually. How much loss would Vidhi have suffered had she given it to Radha for 2 years at 5% per annum on simple interest?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Principal amount (P) = ₹ 8,000

Rate of interest (r) for compound interest and simple interest = 5%

Time period (t) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

For 2 year

D = P × R²/100²

**Solution:**

D = 8000 × 25/(100 × 100)

D = 8000 × 25/(10000)

D = 20

**Therefore, Vidhi would have suffered a loss of approximately ₹20 if she had given the money on simple interest.**

questions.question: There are 50 students in a class. If the ratio of the number of boys to girls is 16 : 9, then what is the mean proportion between the number of boys and girls in the school?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total students = 50

The ratio of boys to girls = 16 ∶ 9

**Concept or Formula used:**

The mean proportional between two numbers 'a' and 'b' is sqrt(a × b).

**Solution:**

⇒ Number of boys = 50 × (16/(16 + 9)) = 32

⇒ Number of girls = 50 × (9/(16 + 9)) = 18

⇒ Mean proportional = √(Number of boys × Number of girls) = √32 × 18 = 24

**Hence, the mean proportion between the number of boys and girls in the school is 24.**

questions.question: A car is travelling at a uniform speed of 51 km/h. The distance travelled by the car from 10:40 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Speed of car = 51 km/h

Travel time = 10:40 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. = 2 hours 20 minutes = 7/3 hours

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

⇒ Distance = 51 km/h × 7/3 hours

**Therefore, the distance traveled by the car from 10:40 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 119 km.**

questions.question: Dinesh offers his customers a discount of 15% on a raincoat and he still makes a profit of 25%. What is the actual cost of the raincoat marketed for Rs.800?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Marked price of raincoat = ₹800

Discount = 15%

Profit = 25%

**Concept or Formula used:**

Selling price after discount = Marked price × (100 - Discount%)/100

Cost price = Selling price / [(100 + Profit%)/100]

**Solution:**

⇒ Selling price after the discount = 800 × (100 - 15)/100 = Rs. 680

⇒ The cost price = 680/[(100 + 25)/100] = 680 × 4/5 = Rs. 544

**Therefore, the actual cost of the raincoat marketed for ₹800 is ₹544.**
